01

Priority

Character Maker

Mid-stage

The core editing path works for selected normal characters.

Available today

Normal male/female cards, asynchronous head 0/200/201 and converted asset selection, shape and color edits, static ABMX, and identity-preserving edited exports. Bounded decoded-rig reuse accelerates repeated normal-head selections while retaining actual byte verification.

Still to complete

Wider catalogs, special and modded assemblies, complete original editing workflows, and remaining owner-thread stalls. First selections still decode and now pay hashing/accounting costs.

Evidence & limitations

In a small Release pair, median warm normal-head selection fell from 667–701 ms to 159–161 ms. First selections cost 16–25 ms more. Logical retained rig payload reached about 39 MB; this is not total RAM or a whole-app benchmark.

Maker contract ↗Card preservation ↗Selection reuse evidence ↗Selection responsiveness #192 ↗

Base Models

Mid-stage

Six normal assemblies have bounded original-player comparisons.

Available today

Female and male heads 0/200/201 have independent neutral and one coupled-shape gates. Head 0 also has bounded bone-type-1 checks for both sexes.

Still to complete

Evidence & limitations

The owning reference records exact model identities, tolerances, original/native hashes and independent neutral repeats.

08

Priority

Plugins

Infancy

A useful bounded execution subset exists; general compatibility is early.

Available today

Translated profiles and three exact-revision native adapters: Mute, StudioAccessoryNames and HideAllUI. Selected mount, cancellation, failure isolation and save/restore workflows are exercised. Native save/reopen now retains queued destruction roots without replaying Awake. Rejected frames restore exact route history, including irregular time steps and lazy-clock ownership.

Still to complete

General DLL, Harmony, coroutine and Unity compatibility, original save adapters, and broader lifecycle coverage. Initialization that changes candidate topology is rejected; library installation retains a separate attachment-read boundary.

Evidence & limitations

Saved-profile restoration permits candidate-owned attachment reads only when initialization leaves the candidate scene unchanged. Metadata inventory does not establish loadability. The queued-destruction change passed 34 Engine tests and 222 app checks in its recorded acceptance. Exact route rollback passes 11 Engine tests and 88 Release app checks; checkpoint timing cost remains unmeasured.

Execution and persistence ↗Native adapters ↗DLL inventory limits ↗

How to read this page

Progress needs context.

This is a reviewed snapshot of accepted work, not a live test dashboard. Linked issues may advance after the review date. Detailed references retain their own measured commits, inputs and exclusions.

Mid-stage

A useful implementation exists, with meaningful gaps in coverage, integration, source semantics or verification.

Infancy

A scaffold or bounded executable subset exists; most original behavior or application integration is still missing.

Performance & fidelity

Responsiveness, total latency, memory and GPU work are assessed separately. Public CI cannot certify private original-player or GPU comparisons.

Ikkoku

Small, continuous updates. Traceable evidence.
